Why Harness Engineering
KEY MODULE OBJECTIVES & GITHUB IMPLEMENTATION

• Examine the 98% Harness Rule in 2026 agentic systems engineering.

• Code Implementation: course_implementation/module_01_why_harness_engineering/harness_vs_model_demo.py
Speed Without Structure Creates Risk: Harness Thesis
The Un-Harnessed Agent Problem
• AI coding agents move fast, but raw model capability without scaffolding creates risk.
• Symptom: Impressive single-turn generation, followed by context amnesia & unverified edits.
• Risk: Infinite execution loops, path traversal exploits, and broken builds.
The Deterministic Harness Solution
• The difference between a useful coding agent and an unreliable one isn't the model alone — it's the harness around it.
• Harness engineering builds surrounding systems that make agent behavior predictable, testable, and constrained.
• Optimizes for trust, correctness, and production readiness rather than raw speed.
Model vs System Harness: The 2026 Paradigm
The Model (Probabilistic Reasoner)
• Generates code proposals based on next-token probability.
• Susceptible to hallucinations, context amnesia, and command retries.
• Requires external scaffolding to verify logic.
The Harness (Deterministic Scaffolding)
• Enforces execution boundaries, AST linting, and path sandboxing.
• Intercepts infinite retry loops automatically.
• Provides standardized LLM client interface for enterprise model providers.
Failure Mode 1: Context Decay & Amnesia
Symptoms of Context Failure
• Agent forgets initial constraints after 8+ conversation turns.
• Mutates unrelated files or reverses prior architecture decisions.
• Mitigation: Persistent memory files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md).
Failure Mode 2: Infinite Execution Loops
Symptoms of Execution Traps
• Agent retries failing compiler command endlessly with minor tweaks.
• Burns tokens without making architectural progress.
• Mitigation: Harness loop detector in harness_vs_model_demo.py.
Failure Mode 3: Unsanitized Mutations & Bad Tools
Symptoms of Dangerous Tool Actions
• Agent attempts rm -rf / or unauthorized shell commands.
• Overwrites production configuration files or drops database tables.
• Mitigation: Pre-action regex shell interceptors & path isolation.

Pillar 1: Memory Files (CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md)

AGENTS.md (Universal Open Standard)

Pillar 2: Scoped Tool & Permission Models
Principle of Least Privilege Execution
• Grant minimal required tools (read_file, write_file, run_test).
• Validate target path resides within workspace root.
• Codebase: core_harness_stack.py validate_tool_permission()
Pillar 3: Deterministic Hooks & Policy Engine
Pre-Execution & Post-Execution Interceptors

• Post-Hooks: Trigger AST static analysis and secret scanners on edits.
Pillars 4 & 5: Context Token Budgeting & Tracing
Context Window Compacting & Budgeting
• Allocate token budget: 20% Memory, 20% Spec, 50% Edit, 10% Output.
• Truncate long compiler outputs while retaining core traceback.
JSONL Observability & Audit Tracing
• Log structured JSON entries for every tool call and error.
• Audit trail logged to events.jsonl for complete telemetry.

Why Prompts Fail & Specs Succeed
The Flaws of Natural Language Prompts
• Prompts are ambiguous, subjective, and context-dependent.
• Lead to feature creep and unrequested refactoring.
The Power of Executable Specifications
• Defines clear contracts, allowed files, and non-goals.
• Codebase: SPEC.md & spec_driven_verifier.py
Anatomy of a Production SPEC.md
Required SPEC.md Structure
• Executive Summary & Problem Context
• Allowed Modification Scope (Explicit file list)
• Explicit Non-Goals (Forbidden actions)
• Input/Output Data Schemas (JSON/TypeScript)
• Machine-Verifiable Acceptance Criteria
Defining Scope Boundaries & Non-Goals
Hard Boundaries to Prevent Scope Creep
• Coding agents tend to refactor adjacent files needlessly.
• SPEC.md lists explicitly allowed files (e.g. auth_validator.py).
• Verifier rejects edits to database.py or config files.
Drafting Machine-Verifiable Acceptance Criteria
Vague vs Executable Criteria
• Vague: Make the API fast and handle errors gracefully.
• Executable: validate_jwt(token) returns {"valid": True} for valid tokens.
• Executable: 100% test coverage in tests/test_auth.py.
How Claude Code Processes Specs
Agent Execution Lifecycle under SDD
• Agent reads SPEC.md at session initialization.
• Agent generates implementation plan matching SPEC criteria.
• Spec verifier audits diff against allowed scope prior to merge.
Spec Verification & Anti-Hallucination Checks
Upfront Consistency Verification
• Run spec validation pass prior to code generation.
• Ensure proposed diff satisfies non-goals and schema constraints.

Guardrails and Deterministic Hooks
KEY MODULE OBJECTIVES & GITHUB IMPLEMENTATION

• Implement path isolation sandboxing and secret key scanning.

The 4-Layer Control Architecture
Layer 1: System Rules (Prompt)
• Soft guidelines defined in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md.
Layer 2: Tool Schemas (JSON Schema)
• Strict argument type & payload shape enforcement.
Layer 3: Interceptors & Hooks (Process)
• Pre-action regex filters & post-action AST static analysis.
Layer 4: OS Sandboxing (System)
• Path traversal blocks & workspace root chroot isolation.
Claude Code Native Hooks & Shell Interception
Hook Events (Exact PascalCase Names)
• Lifecycle: SessionStart, Setup, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, MessageDisplay, Stop, StopFailure, SessionEnd.
• Tools: PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch.
• Agents/tasks: SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle.
• State/context: Notification, InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, PreCompact, PostCompact, Elicitation, ElicitationResult.
settings.json Matcher Shape
• {"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/guard.py","timeout":10}]}]}}
• matcher targets tool names; use Edit|Write for alternation and * (or omit it) to match all.
Post-Action Checks: AST Parsers & Linters
AST Static Analysis & Secret Scanning
• Runs automatically whenever agent writes or updates a file.
• Executes ast.parse() to catch syntax & structural errors.
• Scans for hardcoded secret API keys (sk-proj...).
Filesystem Sandboxing & Path Isolation
Workspace Boundary Enforcement
• Bind agent file operations strictly to project working directory.
• Block path traversal exploits (../../etc/passwd or C:\Windows).
Admin Escalation & Claude Code Permissions
Risk Tiers Mapped to Real Permission Modes
• Lowest mutation risk: plan is read-only exploration.
• Low risk: default runs reads and asks before other tools; add narrow allow rules for trusted reads.
• Reviewed edits: acceptEdits allows working-directory file edits and common filesystem commands; keep risky Bash actions in ask.
• Higher autonomy: auto routes actions through background safety checks; it is a research preview, not a substitute for review.
• Locked automation: dontAsk runs only pre-approved actions and denies anything that would prompt.
• Critical escape hatch: bypassPermissions skips the permission layer; use only inside an isolated container or VM.
settings.json Rules
• {"permissions":{"defaultMode":"default","allow":["Read","Grep"],"ask":["Bash(git push *)"],"deny":["Read(./.env)"]}}
• Rules resolve deny → ask → allow; first matching rule wins.
Evaluation Harnesses: Behavior, Not Just Test Outcomes
Reproducible Agent-Control Evaluation
• Replay fixed tasks from known repository states with explicit acceptance tests.
• Score test results plus scope adherence, denied tool calls, path boundaries, retry budgets, hook decisions, and audit completeness.
• Keep the evaluator independent from the agent and turn every discovered failure into a regression case.
Production Safety & Audit Matrix
Verification Checklist
• [PASS] Are all shell commands logged to audit JSONL with timestamps?
• [PASS] Is secret scanning enforced through PostToolUse or FileChanged hooks?
• [PASS] Is path traversal sandboxing active for all file write tools?

Test-Driven Agent (TDA) Loop Architecture
The TDA Execution Loop
• Write/Identify failing unit test based on SPEC.md.
• Agent generates implementation code to satisfy test.
• Run test runner; extract traceback on failure.
• Feed traceback back into agent repair prompt.
Multi-Tier Testing for Coding Agents
Testing Hierarchy
• Unit Tests: Fast isolation tests verifying individual functions.
• Integration Tests: Verifies multi-module interactions & APIs.
• E2E Tests: Full system workflow verification.
Automated Error Traceback Feedback Loops
Zero-Touch Error Capture
• Eliminates manual copy-pasting of compiler/test errors by developer.
• Harness captures pytest/jest stdout and stderr automatically.
• Passes formatted traceback directly into LLM repair prompt.
Turning Agent Failures into Permanent Tests
Anti-Regression Safeguards
• Every agent hallucination or bug must yield a new regression test.
• Add test case to project regression test suite permanently.
• Codebase: tda_reliability_pipeline.py register_anti_regression_test()
Test Reliability Scorecard & Metrics
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
• First-Pass Pass Rate: % of agent edits passing tests on turn 1.
• Mean Iterations to Repair: Avg attempts to fix failing test (< 3).
• Regression Rate: % of edits breaking existing tests.

Agent Skills Open Standard (SKILL.md)
Folder-Based Skill Encapsulation
• Self-contained folder containing SKILL.md and reference assets.
• YAML frontmatter fields: name, description, allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, context, agent, and model.
• There is no triggers field: description drives discovery and must say what the skill does and when to use it.
• Encapsulates domain expertise and repeatable workflows.
Structuring Skill Instructions & Resources
Skill Directory Anatomy
• SKILL.md: Frontmatter metadata + operational instructions.
• references/: Deep documentation, schema specs, and design rules.
• scripts/: Executable helper scripts and automation tools.
Plugin Bundles: Packaging Capabilities
Deployable Extension Packages
• Bundles skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, LSP servers, and monitors.
• Manifest path: .claude-plugin/plugin.json (name is required; metadata can include description, version, author, and dependencies).
• Distribute through a marketplace.json catalog or load a plugin in place from a skills directory.
Model Context Protocol (MCP) Foundation
Open Standard by Anthropic
• Open standard created by Anthropic for AI-to-system connectivity.
• MCP protocol revisions are dated YYYY-MM-DD; there is no MCP protocol version "2.0".
• JSON-RPC 2.0 is the message framing, not the MCP protocol revision.
• The Python mcp SDK package installed here is 2.0.0; its package version is separate.
• Exposes Tools, Resources, and Prompts to LLMs.
MCP Transports: stdio vs Streamable HTTP
Transport Layer Comparison
• stdio: current transport for local subprocess servers and CLI integrations.
• Streamable HTTP: current remote transport since MCP revision 2025-03-26.
• HTTP+SSE is the deprecated predecessor, not the current remote choice.
MCP Python SDK 2.x vs 1.x
Version-Sensitive Server Class; Shared Authoring Shape
• SDK 2.x (installed mcp 2.0.0): from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
• SDK 2.x: mcp = MCPServer("harness-tools")
• SDK 1.x: from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP; mcp = FastMCP("harness-tools")
• Same in both: @mcp.tool() and @mcp.resource() decorators.
• Same in both: mcp.run(transport="stdio"|"streamable-http"|"sse"); SSE is legacy.
• Codebase: mcp_server_demo.py & mcp_client_runner.py
MCP Governance & Security Controls
Enterprise Governance
• OAuth2 & API Key authentication for remote MCP servers.
• Granular tool-level permission gating (read vs write actions).

Compound Engineering & Agent Teams

Multi-Agent Workflows vs Single Agents
Cognitive Specialization
• Single agents suffer cognitive overload as file count grows.
• Context window bloat reduces reasoning accuracy.
• Multi-agent teams partition responsibilities cleanly.
Role Specialization: Planner Agent
Architect & Requirement Analyst
• Read-only access to codebase; analyzes SPEC.md requirements.
• Drafts high-level architecture & file modification plan.
Role Specialization: Implementer Agent
Constrained Coder Agent
• Receives focused subtask assignment from Planner.
• Executes file edits within strict workspace boundary or Git Worktree.
Role Specialization: Reviewer Agent
Independent Quality Auditor
• Independent agent inspecting Implementer output.
• Runs static analysis, AST linters, and secret scanners.
Subagent Workspace Isolation & Worktrees
First-Class Worktree Isolation
• Define project agents in .claude/agents/<name>.md or personal agents in ~/.claude/agents/<name>.md.
• Set isolation: worktree in the agent frontmatter.
• Claude Code gives that subagent its own git worktree, separating edits from the parent workspace.
Subagent Context Windows & Agent Tool
Focused Context and Delegation
• Each subagent gets its own context window and receives the agent file body as its system prompt.
• Pass only the focused sub-spec and required evidence to the Implementer.
• The Task tool was renamed Agent in Claude Code v2.1.63; Task(...) remains an alias.
• Codebase: multi_agent_team_simulator.py

The 5-Step Practical Workflow Overview
Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
• Spec First (Draft & validate SPEC.md)
• Constrained Execution (Sandboxed agent runner)
• Deterministic Checks (Pre/post hooks & AST linters)
• Test Verification (Automated pytest suite)
• Human Review (Developer sanity check & PR merge)
Phases 1 & 2: Spec First & Constrained Exec
Alignment & Sandboxing
• Align human & AI on exact deliverables before writing code.
• Run agent with minimal tool permissions & strict file scopes.
Phases 3 & 4: Deterministic Checks & Tests
Automated Verification Gating
• Automated AST parsers, linters, & security rule gates.
• Pass unit/integration test suite; feed back any errors.
Phase 5: Human Review & Sanity Auditing
Developer Final Approval
